prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence?
passage: The ranger handed the trail maps to Omar and ____ before the hike began.
choices: I
myself
me
mine
why_wrong: believes "and I" is always the polite, correct form
uses a reflexive pronoun with no matching subject in the sentence
uses a possessive pronoun where an object is needed
explanation: The pronoun is an object of the preposition "to", so the objective case "me" is correct (test it alone: "handed the maps to me"). "I" is subjective, "myself" has no antecedent, and "mine" is possessive.

prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence?
passage: ____ campers who arrived early on Friday got the best spots near the lake.
choices: Us
Our
We
Ourselves
why_wrong: uses the objective case because the pronoun is followed by a noun
treats the pronoun as a possessive describing the campers
uses a reflexive pronoun as the subject
explanation: "___ campers" is the subject of "got", so the subjective "We" is needed (drop "campers": "We got the best spots"). "Us" is objective, "Our" would make the campers belong to someone, and "Ourselves" cannot be a subject.

prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence?
passage: The astronauts repaired the broken solar panel ____, without any help from the control room.
choices: themselves
theirselves
them
themself
why_wrong: builds the pronoun from the possessive "their", a nonstandard form
uses the objective pronoun, which makes the panel seem to belong to or act on someone else
uses a singular form for the plural "astronauts"
explanation: "Themselves" is the intensive pronoun for the plural "astronauts", stressing that they did it on their own. "Theirselves" is nonstandard, "them" is not intensive, and "themself" does not match a plural antecedent.

prompt: Which word or phrase correctly completes the sentence?
passage: When divers explore a deep reef, ____ should carry a light, because colors fade quickly below thirty feet.
choices: you
he or she
we
they
why_wrong: shifts from the third-person "divers" to the second person
shifts from the plural "divers" to a singular pronoun
shifts from "divers" to the first person
explanation: The antecedent "divers" is third person plural, so the pronoun must be "they". "You" and "we" shift person, and "he or she" shifts number.

prompt: Which revision of the sentence is clearest?
passage: When Hana showed Nora the poster, [she] smiled because it had won first prize.
choices: When Hana showed Nora the poster, she smiled because it had won first prize.
When Hana showed Nora the poster, she smiled because she had won first prize.
When Hana showed Nora the poster, Nora smiled because it had won first prize.
When Hana showed Nora the poster, her smile was because it had won first prize.
why_wrong: keeps "she", which could mean either girl
adds a second "she", so now two pronouns are unclear
replaces "she" with "her", which is just as unclear and also awkward
explanation: "She" could refer to Hana or Nora. Naming the person ("Nora smiled") removes the doubt. The other versions keep an unclear "she" or "her".

prompt: Which choice correctly replaces the bracketed word?
passage: Mr. Green and [myself] will chaperone the class trip to the planetarium next week.
choices: myself
me
us
I
why_wrong: keeps a reflexive pronoun as part of the subject because it sounds formal
uses the objective case in the subject
uses a plural pronoun for one person and in the wrong case
explanation: The pronoun is part of the compound subject of "will chaperone", so the subjective "I" is correct ("I will chaperone"). "Myself" has no antecedent, and "me" and "us" are objective.

prompt: Which choice correctly replaces the bracketed word?
passage: When our troop camped at Pine Lake last summer, [you] had to hang every food bag from a high branch.
choices: you
they
one
we
why_wrong: keeps a shift from "our troop" to the second person
shifts to the third person although the writer is in the troop
shifts to an impersonal pronoun in a story about one real trip
explanation: "Our troop" puts the writer in the group, so the pronoun stays first person plural: "we". "You", "they" and "one" shift person.

prompt: Which choice correctly replaces the bracketed word?
passage: The divers checked [their] air tanks twice before jumping off the side of the boat.
choices: its
his or her
our
their
why_wrong: uses a singular pronoun for things, not people
uses a singular pronoun for the plural "divers"
shifts to the first person
explanation: "Divers" is third person plural, so the original "their" is correct. The other choices change number or person.

prompt: Which choice best replaces the bracketed word?
passage: The tent poles were bent and the zipper was broken, and [it] made setting up camp take more than an hour.
choices: it
they
these problems
this
why_wrong: keeps "it", which has no single noun to refer to
uses "they", which seems to point back only to the poles
uses "this" with no noun, leaving the reader to guess what it means
explanation: Two things slowed the campers down, the bent poles and the broken zipper. "These problems" names both. "It", "they" and a bare "this" are vague here.

prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
choices: The guide showed Maya and me the trail to the lookout.
Between you and me, the second campsite had a better view.
Diego and him carried the canoe down to the water.
The ranger gave us hikers a map of the waterfalls.
why_wrong: thinks "me" can never follow "and"
thinks "between you and me" should be "you and I"
thinks "us" cannot come before a noun
explanation: "Him" is part of the subject, so it should be "he" ("He carried the canoe"). "Maya and me" and "you and me" are objects, and "us hikers" is an indirect object, so those are correct.

prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
choices: When we reached the summit, we could see three states.
Every camper must bring a flashlight, and you should pack extra batteries.
If students want to join the astronomy club, they should sign up by Friday.
Our class visited the aquarium, where we watched the sea otters eat.
why_wrong: thinks repeating "we" is an error
thinks "they" cannot refer back to "students"
thinks "our" and "we" are a shift
explanation: The sentence starts with "every camper" (third person) and shifts to "you" (second person); it should say "each camper should pack extra batteries" or similar. The others keep the same person and number.

prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
choices: The captain herself steered the boat through the storm.
Lily taught herself to tie six different knots.
You should give yourself enough time to set up the telescope.
Jack and myself finished the model rocket before dinner.
why_wrong: thinks an intensive pronoun cannot come right after the noun
thinks a reflexive pronoun cannot be an object
thinks "yourself" must refer to someone else in the sentence
explanation: "Myself" needs an antecedent in the sentence; here it is used as a subject, so it should be "Jack and I". The other sentences use intensive or reflexive pronouns correctly.

prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
choices: The telescope arrived on Monday, and Nora set it up that night.
Omar told his father that his bike had a flat tire.
Ben asked Ms. Kim if she could explain the moon's phases again.
The whales surfaced near the boat, and the passengers cheered for them.
why_wrong: thinks "it" is unclear although only the telescope could be set up
thinks "she" is unclear although only Ms. Kim can be meant
thinks "them" could mean the passengers
explanation: "His bike" could be Omar's or his father's, so the pronoun is vague. In the other sentences each pronoun has only one possible antecedent.

prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
choices: Her and her sister built a sandcastle shaped like a whale.
The lifeguard warned Ruby and I about the strong current.
The teacher asked us scientists to label every shell.
Me and Eli collected twelve kinds of seaweed.
why_wrong: uses the objective "her" as a subject
uses the subjective "I" as an object
uses the objective "me" as a subject
explanation: "Us scientists" is the object of "asked", so the objective case is right. The others need "She and her sister", "Ruby and me", and "Eli and I".

prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
choices: When campers hike after dark, you should stay on the marked trail.
Our class planted trees, and you could see the difference by spring.
The scouts packed their bags, and they left before sunrise.
The divers said that a person must check your gear twice.
why_wrong: shifts from "campers" to "you"
shifts from "our class" to "you"
shifts from "a person" to "your"
explanation: "The scouts ... their ... they" keeps the same person and number. Each other sentence shifts to the second person partway through.

prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
choices: The coach gave the trophy to the team and myself.
The boys built the raft by theirselves in one afternoon.
Ivy painted the backdrop herself, using colors she mixed.
Max and me will set up the tent while Dad cooks.
why_wrong: uses "myself" as an object with no antecedent
uses the nonstandard "theirselves"
uses the objective "me" as a subject
explanation: "Herself" correctly stresses that Ivy did the painting. The others need "the team and me", "by themselves", and "Max and I".

prompt: What is the function of the bracketed word in the sentence?
passage: The mayor [herself] cut the ribbon at the opening of the new aquarium.
choices: It receives the action of the verb.
It adds emphasis to the noun right before it.
It shows that the mayor did something to her own body.
It stands for a person the sentence has not named.
why_wrong: takes the pronoun as the object of "cut", though the ribbon is the object
confuses an intensive pronoun with a reflexive one
thinks every pronoun stands for someone not yet named
explanation: "Herself" comes right after "the mayor" and stresses that she, and no one else, cut the ribbon. That is an intensive pronoun; the sentence would still be complete without it.

prompt: In which sentence is the bracketed pronoun intensive rather than reflexive?
choices: Theo cut [himself] on a sharp shell.
Theo bought [himself] a new snorkel.
Theo [himself] found the rare shell.
Theo talked to [himself] while he searched.
why_wrong: thinks any -self pronoun after the verb adds emphasis
does not see that "himself" here is the person Theo bought for
does not see that "himself" here is the object of "to"
explanation: In "Theo himself found the rare shell" the pronoun only adds emphasis and could be removed. In the others it is needed as an object (cut himself, bought himself, talked to himself), so it is reflexive.

prompt: Which best describes the case of the bracketed pronoun?
passage: After the storm, the ranger gave [them] directions to a safer campsite.
choices: subjective
possessive
objective
reflexive
why_wrong: thinks a pronoun near the start of the action is the subject
confuses "them" with "their"
thinks any pronoun referring to people in the sentence is reflexive
explanation: "Them" receives the directions (it is the indirect object of "gave"), so it is in the objective case.

prompt: Which choice best combines the sentences without changing their meaning?
passage: The comet was faint. Astronomers could still see it with a telescope.
choices: Because the comet was so faint, astronomers could still see it with a telescope.
Although the comet was faint, astronomers could still see it with a telescope.
The comet was faint, so astronomers could see it with a telescope.
Astronomers could see the faint comet only without a telescope.
why_wrong: makes faintness the reason they could see it
makes faintness the cause of seeing it and drops the idea of "still"
reverses the fact about the telescope
explanation: "Still" shows that they saw the comet in spite of its faintness, so "although" keeps the meaning. "Because" and "so" turn the faintness into a cause, and the last choice changes the facts.
